sections.title: M&A IT Integration — Two Complete Delivery Playbooks
sections.intro: A full IT-integration control pack from deal restrictions and Day 1 through identity, network, collaboration migrations, application rationalization, hypercare, decommissioning, and benefits—shown once in Agile and once in Predictive / Waterfall.
sections.notice: PMBOK Guide Eighth Edition is approach-neutral. The Predictive / Waterfall playbook is PMBOK 8 aligned; the Agile playbook uses iterative value delivery while retaining fixed legal, security, data, and Day 1 gates.

scenarios.title: M&A IT Integration — Agile Playbook
scenarios.client: Company ABC / Company XYZ — anonymized fictional scenario
scenarios.role: M&A IT Technical Project Manager — Agile integration lead
scenarios.summary: Integrate Company XYZ into Company ABC through outcome-based releases: secure Day 1 employee experience, identity and network bridges, Google Workspace/Slack/Asana/Jira migration, application rationalization, hypercare, and controlled convergence.
scenarios.decision: Continue the migration release plan; hold the Jira production cohort until automation regression passes, close 15 Day 1 exceptions, and preserve source retention until legal-hold validation is accepted.

metrics.label: Applications discovered
metrics.note: Every app requires owner and disposition

scenarios.financial_note: All amounts are fictional planning assumptions. The Agile forecast is refreshed from accepted increments, vendor commitments, remaining backlog, reserve, and identified uncertainty. No projected license reduction is a realized saving until Finance validates the stopped invoice or contract.

risks.risk: Identity duplicates or stale contractor records block Day 1 access
risks.response: Roster reconciliation at T-10/T-3/T-0; named exception path.

risks.risk: Overlapping subnets disrupt routing or DNS
risks.response: Collision register, NAT/renumber, isolated test, route-withdrawal rollback.

risks.risk: Collaboration permissions, retention, or integrations differ after migration
risks.response: Identity-first mapping, legal review, pilot, counts/samples/permission validation.

risks.risk: Fifteen workers remain on controlled Day 1 exceptions
risks.response: Tested workarounds, named owners/expiry, daily burn-down and manager communication.

scenarios.client: Company ABC / Company XYZ — anonymized fictional scenario
scenarios.role: M&A IT Technical Project Manager — Predictive integration lead
scenarios.summary: Deliver the same Company ABC/XYZ integration through formal scope, WBS, schedule and cost baselines; staged design, Day 1, migration, decommission, and closeout gates; integrated change control; quality assurance; and earned value reporting.
scenarios.decision: Maintain the Week 24 baseline and hold Jira production release. Use available schedule float for the collaboration recovery plan; do not reduce validation, rollback, or legal-hold controls to improve SPI.

sections.title: Desktop, Laptop, and Phone Refresh — Four Complete Delivery Playbooks
sections.intro: One 360-device, four-site program with a shared technical/control pack and four distinct operating systems: Kanban, Scrum, Predictive / Waterfall, and Hybrid. Each has its own dashboard, planning artifacts, metrics, and executive status.
sections.notice: All four methods use the same mandatory endpoint, data, security, asset, sanitization, procurement, user, support, and closeout controls. Method selection changes how work is planned and governed—not whether those controls exist.

scenarios.title: Enterprise Hardware Refresh — Kanban Playbook
scenarios.client: Company ABC / Company XYZ — anonymized fictional scenario
scenarios.role: Technical Project Manager — Kanban hardware refresh lead
scenarios.summary: Run the 360-device, four-site refresh as a pull system with WIP limits, service classes, explicit policies, aging and cycle-time evidence, while retaining full security, data, asset, sanitization, support, and closure controls.
scenarios.decision: Stop starting standard work; direct capacity to the 16 exception and remote-return items while preserving WIP limits and custody controls.
scenarios.financial_note: All values are fictional planning assumptions. The $792K authorization and $748.4K forecast require real purchase orders, invoices, labor, tax/shipping, credits, warranty, and reserve approvals before use. User productivity or released capacity is not cash savings without Finance validation.

risks.risk: Critical application, driver, VPN, or peripheral fails on the new build
risks.response: Persona pilot, versioned package, fallback, and owner acceptance.

risks.risk: Local or application data is not protected before retirement
risks.response: Precheck, approved backup/KFM, validation, and sanitization hold.

risks.risk: Sixteen application, accessibility, leave, or logistics exceptions remain
risks.response: Named owners/dates/workarounds; specialized capacity and weekly steering.

risks.risk: Returned-device custody or sanitization evidence is incomplete
risks.response: Serial scans, secure storage, evidence validation, and quarantine.

Specialized personas and remote returns need explicit capacity and earlier discovery

scenarios.title: Enterprise Hardware Refresh — Scrum Playbook
scenarios.client: Company ABC / Company XYZ — anonymized fictional scenario
scenarios.role: Technical Project Manager — Scrum hardware refresh lead
scenarios.summary: Deliver the same refresh through one Product Goal, an ordered Product Backlog, nine two-week Sprints, working accepted device/user/asset Increments, reviews, retrospectives, and a strict Definition of Done.
scenarios.decision: Keep 16 exception PBIs in the Product Backlog, allocate Sprint 9 to specialized closure, and do not count deferred items in the Increment.
